original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Pin matched present-head flag 1 (X0 to Y7, basis head 232) from the #2981 certificate and prove on the published #1991 channel that the basis head enters Y7's frame, both as a listed vector and in the GF(2) span, only at Y7's terminal transport after-frame (event 3473), after all six Y7 row updates have run in head-free charts, while X0's span keeps the head at every annotation. No Y7 event occurs while both endpoint frames host the head direction, so chronological dirty restoration cannot use co-hosted basis-head geometry on this word.
scope_change_reason: Open #3349 registers the 208-flag restoration census and names the present-head class (0, 1, 9, 43). Open #3443 pins flag 9 with literal frame membership. Open #3392 pins absent-head flag 2. Open #3363/#3365/#3371/#3372 cover algebraic coefficient delivery concentrated on flag 0. Flag 1 is the next present-head member outside those packages. Its numbers differ from flag 9 (drop 591, arrive 3473, gap 2882), so it is not a reprint. Because the native channel's frames are binary subspaces with nested transports, this package also checks hosting in span: the literal source drop is a chart change, and the obstruction is entirely on the target side.
bottleneck_link: A present-head target final does not host the basis-head direction while the target is still being updated. On flag 1 every Y7 row update precedes the head's entry into Y7's span, and Y7 has no event after that entry, so a dirty restoration using co-hosted geometry needs new target events.
stop_rule: Stop after flag 1's late-only hosting obstruction is pinned literally and in span and dual-scanned. Do not build a correction word, recompute algebraic relays, or certify flags 0, 9 or 43.
evidence: Flag 1 is source 0, target 7, basis head 232. X0 starts at [232]; its first transport at event 591 goes to [8, 32, 64, 128, 256], removing 232 from the list but not from the span (232 = 8 xor 32 xor 64 xor 128). All 22 X0 annotations span the head. Y7's preterminal frames are [], [95] and [95, 486], whose spans exclude 232. The head enters Y7 only in the after-frame of event 3473, Y7's last event (literal gap 2882 after event 591). Y7's six adds (events 19, 20, 2013, 2146, 2526, 2797) all run in head-free charts. No joint X0/Y7 event exists; all eight endpoint transports are nested upward with rank steps equal to their recorded costs. Neither endpoint frame is restored (ranks 1 to 9 and 0 to 8). Selected kappa is unchanged.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for derivation, implementation, checking and writing.

open_questions.question: Can a changed schedule place 232 in Y7's span before Y7's last row update, while X0 is still live, and what does that add to the channel bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: On the published word the head direction reaches Y7 only at its final transport, after the last add at event 2797. A repair must move a rank step of Y7 earlier or add target events, and both cost transports.
open_questions.first_step: Try moving part of Y7's rank-six terminal step (event 3473) ahead of the add at event 2797 so that 232 is in span there. Then check the common-chart requirement against D17's frame at that add.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package reads only the published frames of flag 1. It does not construct a repair, price one, or check D17's frame contract.

open_questions.question: Do the other present-head flags show the same pattern in span: the source keeps the head direction throughout and the target gains it only at its terminal transport?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Open #3443 states flag 9's source drop as literal membership. If spans behave as they do on flag 1, the present-head obstruction is a target-side property, and a changed schedule only needs earlier target hosting.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun this package's span check on flags 9 and 43 against the same pinned inputs. Do not touch flag 0, which belongs to the coefficient cascade.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package certifies flag 1 only. Flag 9 is the subject of open #3443.
